facts.text: Water View sits on the Rappahannock River, just 6.4 miles north‑northwest of Urbanna, where the river’s tides shape the low‑lying landscape.
The community’s name reflects its waterfront setting, with elevations ranging only 10 to 26 feet above sea level, making tides a daily influence.
Water View’s history dates back to the Rappahannock Indian Tribe, part of the Powhatan Confederacy, who first inhabited the area before European arrival.
In 1608, Captain John Smith’s expedition first charted the Chesapeake Bay near what is now Water View, where a stingray bite was treated with local herbal remedies.
The surrounding marshes support vital wildlife, serving as nurseries for menhaden and blue crabs and breeding grounds for prothonotary warblers and bald eagles.
A post office operated in Water View until March 8, 2008, marking the end of a long‑standing local institution.
